description: The PLAN Q10 sensitivity analysis, registered before any variant was computed. Every variant listed here is computed and reported; none is adopted, and no variant is named best. The frozen model in `frozen` remains the reported result.

unresolved_defaults.why: The value a factor takes when it could not be resolved or was not declared. The S4 handoff names this the most consequential sweep: an unresolved finding outranks a resolved one of the same risk, because the defaults are conservative.
unresolved_defaults.note: Each list is a factor's whole range, so no value is selected. The frozen value in each list is the identity and is not counted as a variant. Exposure 2 to 5 is the sweep rubric.json itself registers for the one factor whose unresolved policy is sensitivity-analysed; the networking scenario is reported by name across it, as the S2 handoff's item 12 requires.

band_boundaries.why: Where a score becomes a band. Corpus v1 sets expected_band nowhere, so this shows how the distribution shifts and validates no boundary.
band_boundaries.note: No score changes, so no ordering metric can.

weights.why: Equal weighting is a declared neutral baseline, not a claim that the six factors matter equally (PLAN Q10).

likelihood_weighted.motivation: The likelihood axis of the OWASP Risk Rating Methodology and the exploitability metrics of CVSS v3.1: how reachable the resource is and how much authority it carries.

impact_weighted.motivation: The impact axis of the OWASP Risk Rating Methodology and the impact assessment of NIST SP 800-30 Rev.1: what the asset holds and how much the environment matters.

weights.note: Bands are not reported for a weighted variant. The four bands are positioned against the 1-28 ceiling, a weighted sum has a different ceiling, and rescaling the boundaries to fit it would define a new model. Weighted variants are judged on ordering alone. The two named weightings were proposed from sources the rubric already cites and approved by the project author; they are not presented as independently expert-derived.

low_confidence_threshold.why: How many of the five contextual factors may be defaulted or unresolved before a finding is low-confidence. Frozen at 3 by S3b before any scoring output existed.
low_confidence_threshold.note: No score changes. Only the low-confidence count and the clean subsets move.

reported_for_each_variant: the Critical/High/Medium/Low counts over the findings the framework makes a quality claim about (unweighted variants only)
how many of those findings changed band and how many changed score
Kendall's tau-b between the frozen ranking and the variant's over the same findings
contrastive pairs passed under the registered case rule, and which failed
scenario exact tier matches and the ordered case pairs right, tied and inverted, with each scenario's ordering
the low-confidence count, and the clean pair and scenario subsets
rules: The plan is committed before any variant is computed, and a test checks that order against git.
At the frozen settings the recomputation must reproduce every committed score, band and low-confidence flag exactly, or the analysis refuses to run.
Every registered variant is computed and written to the artifact. There is no filtering step.
No variant replaces the frozen model anywhere in the evaluation record.
The baseline is not varied: it is the fixed comparator, banded at the frozen settings.
